speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing neck and arm pain along with paresthesias and muscle weakness; can you tell me specifically where the pain is located and whether it radiates down your arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy.

The clinical presentation of progressive bilateral hand weakness, paresthesias, and burning neck pain in a 58-year-old male with a history of diabetes and prior trauma is highly suggestive of cervical spinal cord compression due to degenerative changes. Given the severity of the motor deficits, I will request imaging to confirm the level and extent of cord compression. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI.
